title: Gestures, permissions and app states in tests

videos.script: A person does not click an app. They tap it, hold a finger on it, swipe it and turn it sideways. {{touch}} And the app does not stay on the screen. A call arrives, the person goes to another app, and Android may stop Tickets to free memory while it waits. {{life}} Then there is what the app is allowed to do. Since Android 13, Tickets may not send a reminder until the person says yes, and they can say no. {{permission}} Each of these is a path a manual tester follows by hand. This lesson makes them paths a test can follow. {{paths}} First, gestures. A swipe is not a command of its own. It is a finger put down, moved and lifted, and you will see exactly that sent to Appium. {{gestures}} Then the permission dialog. It belongs to Android, not to the app, and that decides which tool can answer it. {{dialog}} Then the app's states. What Tickets keeps when it is sent away and killed, read from its own code, and the tests that check it. {{states}} And last, the interruptions a phone throws at an app, and which of them are worth a test. {{interruptions}}
